title: Dominic and the Ledger
premise: In 1792, in the river town of Vellamont, Dominic Yarrow — a typeface cutter's daughter who has lived as her father's 'son' since his death — keeps the print shop's ledger, which holds every debt, alias, and secret name in town. When the revolutionary army requisitions the town, the ledger becomes evidence of treason against neighbors she loves, and the new commandant orders it burned. Dominic steals it instead, and over nine winter days must move the book past three checkpoints with help from Ilse, an army cartographer torn between duty and desire. The story ends at the century's turn: Dominic delivers the ledger to the printers' guild tribunal, saving forty-one names but losing the shop, her father's type, and nearly her own life — and chooses exile with Ilse rather than a pardon that would require renouncing what she did.
about_author: Casper Almeida is the pen name of a former letterpress apprentice who spent a decade restoring nineteenth-century printing equipment in coastal mill towns. Their fiction has appeared in small journals devoted to working-class history.

chapters.title: The Weight of Lead
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. A ordinary day in the Yarrow print shop: setting type, mending the ledger, dodging the landlady's questions about why 'Master Yarrow' never shows his face. Establishes the double life and the ledger as the shop's true heart. Emotional beat: quiet contentment built on concealment.

chapters.title: Names in Ink
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. She updates the ledger — debts forgiven quietly, aliases recorded for townsfolk hiding from old warrants — revealing how much of Vellamont's survival runs through her hands. Beat: pride shadowed by the fear of being discovered herself.

chapters.title: Drums on the Ferry Road
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The revolutionary army arrives; officers requisition warehouses, billet soldiers, and post a proclamation demanding all commercial records be surrendered within three days. Beat: the world she thought happened elsewhere arrives at the door.

chapters.title: The Commandant's List
chapters.summary: Commandant Ravel's POV. Ravel, methodical and weary, explains to his aide why the ledger matters: names are how revolutions eat their own tails. He wants it burned as an act of mercy. Beat: chilling reasonableness.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Neighbors beg her to hide their entries; the baker offers bribes, the widow Marchand offers threats. Dominic copies nothing — there's no time — and realizes the original book is the only copy of forty-one lives. Beat: panic hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What Her Father Cut
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV, with flashback. Memory of her father teaching her to cut type and telling her ink outlives men; she hollows the shop's proofing press to fit the ledger. Beat: grief repurposed into craft.

chapters.title: Surrender Day
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The army collects every record in town while the hollowed press sits in plain view. A sergeant lingers near it; Dominic talks her way through by correcting his French grammar. Beat: terror wearing competence like a mask.

chapters.title: The Cartographer
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse Brandt, mapping the occupied town, notices the print shop's dimensions don't match its tax record. She visits, says almost nothing, leaves. Beat: curiosity sharpening into suspicion — and something warmer.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Bridge
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. First attempt to move the ledger, sewn into a bolt of sailcloth, fails when the bridge closes for a search. She retreats and hides the book in a grave niche overnight. Beat: humiliation and cold dread.

chapters.title: A Debt Repaid in Bread
chapters.summary: Widow Marchand's POV. Marchand, whose forged name is in the ledger, covers for Dominic during questioning but makes clear the favor will be called back. Beat: solidarity with teeth.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Two: The Customhouse
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Second attempt, disguised as a delivery clerk, gets her inside the customhouse before Ravel institutes body searches after a smuggling bust. She escapes through the cooperage. Beat: hope clipped short.

chapters.title: Ilse Draws the Shop
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Mapping again, Ilse measures the print shop and finds the hidden cavity behind the press. She confronts Dominic alone — and instead of reporting her, asks one question: whose names? Beat: the turn from suspicion to complicity.

chapters.title: Two Kinds of Duty
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse weighs her oath against what she read in the ledger's open page: her own brother's name, pardoned years ago by a bribe recorded in Dominic's careful hand. Beat: love and duty beginning to pull apart.

chapters.title: The Burn Order
chapters.summary: Ravel's POV. Pressured from above to produce traitors before the new year, Ravel reverses himself: the ledger will now be used, not burned. He orders the print shop sealed. Beat: mercy curdling into necessity.

chapters.title: Sealed Doors
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Soldiers seal the shop with the hollowed press — and the ledger — inside. Dominic watches her whole life nailed shut. Beat: despair at its lowest ebb.

chapters.title: Night Work
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse forges a requisition order authorizing removal of 'printing equipment' to the garrison, planning to extract the ledger herself. Beat: first open act of betrayal against her own side.

chapters.title: The Unsealing
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Under Ilse's forged order, they open the shop at night; soldiers nearly catch them mid-extraction. They get the ledger out but must leave the press broken behind them. Beat: partnership sealed under threat.

chapters.title: What the Book Costs
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Hiding in the tannery loft, Dominic reads the ledger fully for the first time and finds her father's own entry — a payment made to keep her secret. Beat: identity shaken; gratitude and rage entwined.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: The Gate
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The final checkpoint guards the north gate, and Ravel has posted her description — not as a woman, but as 'the Yarrow boy.' The disguise that hid her now hunts her. Beat: irony turned to trap.

chapters.title: Ravel Suspects
chapters.summary: Ravel's POV. Ravel reviews the requisition forgery and recognizes Ilse's hand from her maps. He says nothing, sets watchers, and waits. Beat: the noose drawn slowly.

chapters.title: The Tannery Smell
chapters.summary: Marchand's POV. Marchand discovers the hiding place and, seeing leverage, goes to sell the information — then hesitates at the garrison door, remembering the ledger forgave her. Beat: betrayal interrupted by grace.

chapters.title: A Map With Two Routes
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse drafts two escape routes — one safe for the book, one safe for Dominic — knowing they can't both survive. She gives Dominic the choice without telling her it's a choice. Beat: love expressed as terrible honesty.

chapters.title: The River Road
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic takes the book route alone, wading the frozen shallows past the gate, pursued by dogs. She twists an ankle and shelters in a ferryman's hut. Beat: endurance stripped to animal stubbornness.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ravel arrests Ilse and questions her gently, offering her brother's safety in exchange for the ledger's location. Beat: temptation framed as kindness.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Price
chapters.summary: Ferryman Odile's POV. An old smuggler, Odile recognizes what Dominic carries and demands a page of the ledger as payment — her own expunged debt. Dominic refuses; Odile helps anyway. Beat: honor among the compromised.

chapters.title: What Ilse Chose
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse gives up a false location, buying Dominic two days, and accepts transfer to the penal column. Beat: sacrifice without martyrdom — she expects to survive it.

chapters.title: The Guild House
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic reaches the printers' guild tribunal in the city, but the guild elders hesitate: ruling for the ledger means defying the army. Beat: sanctuary that isn't.

chapters.title: Century's Eve
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, brief interlocking scenes. New Year's Eve across Vellamont: Ravel drafting charges, Marchand lighting candles, Ilse marching, Dominic waiting outside the tribunal hall as snow falls. Beat: held breath before the century turns.

chapters.title: The Reading of Names
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The tribunal convenes at midnight; Dominic argues not law but memory — reading forty-one names aloud until the room stops being a courtroom. Beat: the climax's moral force.

chapters.title: Ravel's Verdict
chapters.summary: Ravel's POV. Ordered to seize the tribunal, Ravel instead testifies that the ledger's records are accurate — damning his own superiors' earlier pardons-for-sale. Beat: the antagonist choosing justice outside his chain of command.

chapters.title: Forty-One
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The tribunal rules the ledger admissible; the amnesty holds for thirty-nine names. Two cannot be saved, and Dominic must tell Marchand one of them is hers. Beat: victory with a wound in it.

chapters.title: The Pardon Offered
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. The new authorities offer Dominic a full pardon — contingent on surrendering the ledger permanently and denying Ilse's involvement. Beat: the price of survival named aloud.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Shop
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic returns to find the print shop burned in reprisal, her father's type melted. She gathers a single surviving letterform — a lowercase d — from the rubble. Beat: mourning made tangible.

chapters.title: The Penal Column Road
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse, marching north, learns the ledger survived and that someone is petitioning for her release. Beat: hope arriving as rumor.

chapters.title: Ledger Closed
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. At the guild archive, Dominic formally closes the ledger, entering final entries: debts settled, names cleared, her father's secret recorded honestly at last. Beat: reconciliation with inheritance.

chapters.title: Terms of Exile
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. Dominic declines the pardon, trading it for Ilse's release papers — choosing the road over protection. Beat: love against duty resolved in action.

chapters.title: Northbound
chapters.summary: Shared POV. Ilse and Dominic reunite at the city gate with nothing but the letterform d, Ilse's maps, and forged passes. Beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: The Century Turns
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. On the road north, news reaches them: the old regime is falling, and the ledger is being printed as evidence in trials far away. History, it turns out, was happening to them all along. Beat: awe and vertigo.

chapters.title: A New Hand
chapters.summary: Dominic's POV. In a border town, Dominic takes work cutting type under a new name and begins a fresh ledger — blank pages, honest entries. Beat: quiet rebirth.

chapters.title: Epilogue: What Outlives Men
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV, years later. Ilse finds the old ledger in a published trial record, her brother's name vindicated in print, and brings it home to Dominic. Final line echoes the father: ink outlives men. Beat: peace earned, not given.
